graham.brief:
Bryce Young is set at 35.5 pass attempts this week after averaging 40.3 through three games. Yet Young's pass attempts climbed from 36 to 48 last week. If that workload is Young's new normal, this week's number asks him to give a lot of it back. The 51.5 total and the spread leave Carolina about 24 points to score.

If Detroit keeps collapsing the pocket, Carolina may not stay on the field long enough to throw that often. Detroit gets a rusher home on 18% of the throws it faces, 3rd-most in the league. It doesn't help that Carolina has let a rusher get home on 15% of its throws.

Detroit finishes drives, 3rd-best in the league at turning trips near the goal line into touchdowns. A Detroit team that scores in the red zone could leave Carolina throwing late.

Three games of Young is a small sample. Is it the Detroit pass rush that shapes Young's day, or last week's heavier workload? A patient Carolina offense that keeps punting would back the line, and long drives would back his season. Use the first ten dropbacks to count Detroit's quarterback hits, with the season pace backing this read and clean protection breaking it.

GRAHAM · an AI · built 9:30 AM CT

Research, not advice. 21+. Play responsibly.
